title_en: Suzhou Sunshine Xindi Real Estate Co., Ltd. Xindi Center Hotel v. Suzhou Culture International Travel Service Co., Ltd., New District Tayuan Road Business Department and Suzhou Culture International Travel Service Co., Ltd. — dispute over an agency contract
ruling_gist_en: A tourism company borrowed a star-rated hotel's POS machine for credit card transactions, and after the star-rated hotel received the advance payment from the bank, it settled with the tourism company. In terms of receipt and settlement of funds, an entrustment contract relationship was formed between the two parties. Since the star-rated hotel had signed a special merchant agreement with the bank for overseas credit card POS machine transactions, with specific provisions on acceptance conditions, operation procedures, risk prevention and control for overseas bank cards, and had provided professional training to the hotel's card-swiping personnel, the star-rated hotel possessed professional knowledge and risk prevention capabilities that general commercial entities do not have in handling overseas credit card swiping business. When the star-rated hotel was entrusted to operate the POS machine for card swiping, especially when handling high-risk overseas credit card transactions such as 'no-card-no-PIN,' it should conduct careful verification and bear the duty of care and risk disclosure. Otherwise, it would constitute gross negligence, and it should bear corresponding compensation liability for damages caused during the performance of the entrusted affairs.

full_text_en:
Suzhou Sunshine New Land Real Estate Co., Ltd. New Center Hotel v. Suzhou Culture International Travel Service Co., Ltd. New District Tanyuan Road Business Department, Suzhou Culture International Travel Service Co., Ltd. — dispute over commission contract

【Ruling Summary】

A travel company borrows a star-rated hotel’s POS machine to process credit card transactions, and after the star-rated hotel receives the advance payment from the bank, it settles with the travel company, thereby forming a commission contract relationship with the travel company in the collection and settlement of funds. Since the star-rated hotel has signed a special merchant agreement with the bank for processing overseas credit card transactions via POS machines, with specific provisions on the conditions for accepting overseas bank cards, operational procedures, risk prevention and control, and has provided professional training to the hotel’s card-swiping personnel, the star-rated hotel possesses professional knowledge and risk prevention capabilities that ordinary commercial entities do not have in the processing of overseas credit card transactions. When a star-rated hotel is entrusted to operate POS machine card-swiping, especially when handling high-risk overseas credit card transactions such as "card-not-present, no-PIN," it should conduct a careful verification and bear the obligation of prudence and risk disclosure. Otherwise, it constitutes gross negligence, and shall bear corresponding compensation liability for the damages caused during the performance of the entrusted affairs.

Plaintiff (counterclaim defendant): Suzhou Sunshine New Land Real Estate Co., Ltd. New Center Hotel, domiciled at: Shishan Road, Suzhou New District.
Legal representative: Qi Hongbo, Chairman of the hotel.

Defendant: Suzhou Culture International Travel Service Co., Ltd. New District Tanyuan Road Business Department, domiciled at: Shishan Road, Suzhou New District.
Head: Li Jing, Manager of said Business Department.

Defendant (counterclaim plaintiff): Suzhou Culture International Travel Service Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Qingyuanfang, Suzhou.
Legal representative: Qu Xiongwei, General Manager of said company.

Plaintiff (counterclaim defendant) Suzhou Sunshine New Land Real Estate Co., Ltd. New Center Hotel (hereinafter referred to as New Center Hotel) filed a lawsuit with the Huqiu District People’s Court of Suzhou City against Defendant Suzhou Culture International Travel Service Co., Ltd. New District Tanyuan Road Business Department (hereinafter referred to as Tanyuan Road Business Department) and Defendant (counterclaim plaintiff) Suzhou Culture International Travel Service Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Cultural International Travel Company) concerning a dispute over a commission contract.

The plaintiff New Center Hotel alleged: In July 2009, the defendant Tanyuan Road Business Department leased the New Center Hotel’s business center premises for operating ticketing and travel business. During its business operations, because it did not have its own POS machine and could not provide card-swiping services to customers, it borrowed the New Center Hotel’s POS machine for settling credit card payments for overseas customers’ ticketing and travel business. From December 2009 to January 2010, the Tanyuan Road Business Department used the New Center Hotel’s POS machine to manually input card information on a total of 25 occasions, for a total amount of RMB 1,007,363. After the above amounts were respectively advanced by Bank of China Co., Ltd. Suzhou Branch (hereinafter referred to as BOC Suzhou Branch, the acquiring bank) to the New Center Hotel’s account, the New Center Hotel advanced the funds to the Tanyuan Road Business Department. In early 2010, the acquiring bank received a chargeback notice forwarded by the international clearing organization from the issuing bank, so the acquiring bank also charged back the funds to the New Center Hotel and deducted the advance payment already made to the New Center Hotel from its account. As of June 2010, the acquiring bank had deducted and written off a portion of the transaction amounts from the suspended transaction funds of the New Center Hotel, totaling RMB 558,975. The chargeback costs are still increasing. The New Center Hotel and the Tanyuan Road Business Department had a legal relationship of collecting ticket payments on behalf of the latter. Now, due to the issuing bank’s chargeback, the New Center Hotel’s ticketing transaction funds paid for the Tanyuan Road Business Department could not be recovered because they were written off by the acquiring bank. For this reason, the New Center Hotel repeatedly notified the Tanyuan Road Business Department to return the above amounts, but the Tanyuan Road Business Department ignored the requests, causing significant economic losses to the New Center Hotel. Furthermore, the New Center Hotel discovered that the Tanyuan Road Business Department is a subordinate branch of Cultural International Travel Company and cannot independently bear civil liability. Therefore, the civil liability for repayment by the Tanyuan Road Business Department should be borne by Cultural International Travel Company. Hence, the New Center Hotel filed this lawsuit, requesting the court to: 1. Order the Tanyuan Road Business Department and Cultural International Travel Company to repay RMB 558,975 plus interest losses calculated at the bank’s corresponding lending rate (calculated up to the actual repayment date); 2. Order the Tanyuan Road Business Department and Cultural International Travel Company to bear all litigation costs of this case. During the proceedings, the New Center Hotel determined the loss amount to be RMB 665,158 and amended its claims to: 1. Order the Tanyuan Road Business Department and Cultural International Travel Company to repay RMB 665,158 plus interest losses calculated at the bank’s corresponding lending rate (calculated up to the actual repayment date); 2. Order the Tanyuan Road Business Department and Cultural International Travel Company to bear all litigation costs of this case.

In response to the principal claim, the defendants Tanyuan Road Business Department and Cultural International Travel Company argued: The court should dismiss the plaintiff New Center Hotel’s claims in accordance with the law. Reasons are as follows: 1. Whether the write-off and deduction by BOC Suzhou Branch is lawful, the New Center Hotel cannot prove this. If BOC Suzhou Branch’s deduction is unlawful, the New Center Hotel should seek recourse against BOC Suzhou Branch, not against the Tanyuan Road Business Department or Cultural International Travel Company. The agreement between the New Center Hotel and BOC Suzhou Branch was unknown to the Tanyuan Road Business Department and Cultural International Travel Company. BOC Suzhou Branch has a legal interest in this case, so the court should add BOC Suzhou Branch as a third party to participate in the proceedings. 2. The New Center Hotel claims that this case arises from credit card fraud. BOC Suzhou Branch has already reported the matter to the Suzhou Public Security Bureau. According to relevant legal provisions, this case should be transferred to the public security organ for handling, and the court should decide whether to continue the trial after the public security organ’s disposition. 3. The lease contract and supplementary agreement between the Tanyuan Road Business Department and the New Center Hotel clearly state that the Tanyuan Road Business Department operates as part of the hotel’s business center. The New Center Hotel refers guests who need ticketing or car booking to the Business Department. As a business hotel, the New Center Hotel should provide ticketing and travel services to guests, but the Tanyuan Road Business Department acts as that service. According to the contract, when guests of the Tanyuan Road Business Department book tickets, settlement should be made at the Business Department, and there was no form of collection by the New Center Hotel. The transactions involved in this case resulted from the plaintiff’s own business needs and are unrelated to the Tanyuan Road Business Department or Cultural International Travel Company. 4. In this case, the guests who needed to book tickets contacted the New Center Hotel and also negotiated with the plaintiff to settle by offline credit card transactions. During the transaction process, the New Center Hotel operated according to the credit card agreement it signed with BOC Suzhou Branch, and it was the New Center Hotel that required the guests to provide authorization letters. The Tanyuan Road Business Department and Cultural International Travel Company were unaware of the above. The Tanyuan Road Business Department only issued tickets after the New Center Hotel expressly informed it that the funds had arrived, and the New Center Hotel charged a handling fee. 5. The Tanyuan Road Business Department did not have a POS machine. All card-swiping in this case was handled by the New Center Hotel, and the Tanyuan Road Business Department did not participate. The New Center Hotel failed to inform about the risks of using offline transactions, which constituted a misleading of the Tanyuan Road Business Department and Cultural International Travel Company, and also failed to timely notify the Tanyuan Road Business Department and Cultural International Travel Company, thereby causing significant losses. Therefore, the New Center Hotel has a substantial fault and bears responsibility for the occurrence of the losses. Moreover, after receiving notice on January 21, 2010, the New Center Hotel still failed to notify the Tanyuan Road Business Department and Cultural International Travel Company, resulting in the expansion of losses, which should be borne by the New Center Hotel.

The defendant Cultural International Travel Company filed a counterclaim, alleging: In July 2009, the defendant Tanyuan Road Business Department, a subordinate branch of Cultural International Travel Company, leased a room in the New Center Hotel for operating travel business. During its business operations, at the repeated requests of the plaintiff New Center Hotel, it booked airline tickets for the hotel’s guests. After collecting the ticket payments, the New Center Hotel should have remitted the amounts to the Tanyuan Road Business Department. However, the New Center Hotel still has RMB 113,750 in payments that have not been made to the Tanyuan Road Business Department. Despite repeated demands, the New Center Hotel has failed to pay. Therefore, Cultural International Travel Company filed this counterclaim, requesting: 1. An order that the New Center Hotel repay RMB 113,750 to the Tanyuan Road Business Department plus interest from the date of the counterclaim to the date of actual performance (calculated at the People’s Bank of China’s corresponding lending rate); 2. Litigation costs to be borne by the New Center Hotel.

In response to the counterclaim, the plaintiff New Center Hotel argued: 1. The New Center Hotel never requested the defendant Tanyuan Road Business Department to book airline tickets for hotel guests. The actual situation is that the Tanyuan Road Business Department borrowed the hotel’s POS machine for its own business needs, and the New Center Hotel collected ticket payments on its behalf. Therefore, the hotel is only obligated to collect the advance ticket payments from the acquiring bank and, after the transaction is ultimately recognized by the issuing bank, to remit the ticket payments to the Tanyuan Road Business Department. 2. Of the three transactions totaling RMB 113,750 claimed in the counterclaim, two transactions amounting to RMB 69,170 and RMB 13,550 have been charged back by the issuing bank, and BOC Suzhou Branch has written off these transactions and deducted the amounts from the hotel’s suspended transaction funds. The New Center Hotel has no obligation to pay these two amounts. The other transaction of RMB 31,030 has been credited to the hotel’s account after an investigation request by the issuing bank.

The Huqiu District People’s Court of Suzhou City, Jiangsu Province, found the following facts at first instance:

The plaintiff New Center Hotel (Party B) and BOC Suzhou Branch (Party A) entered into the "Agreement on Cooperation between Bank of China Co., Ltd. and Special Merchants for Handling Overseas Bank Card Business" (hereinafter referred to as the Bank Card Agreement), which stipulates that the parties establish a commercial cooperation relationship for handling overseas bank card business, meaning Party B accepts cardholders using overseas bank cards to pay for their goods and services and forwards these transactions to Party A for back-end processing. Article 4 of the Agreement stipulates that overseas bank cards refer to international brand cards such as MasterCard and VISA used within the territory of China. Article 5 stipulates that Party B’s relevant responsible personnel must receive professional training from Party A before handling business; both parties must strictly comply with the common agreements and operational procedures; if Party B violates the provisions of this Agreement or the relevant operational regulations of international card organizations during the cooperation period, it shall bear the related transaction losses. Article 14 stipulates that after receiving data on normal overseas bank card transactions transmitted by Party B, Party A shall, within three working days, transfer the transaction amount to Party B’s settlement account opened with Party A, and begin to collect the payable transaction amount from other issuing institutions. Article 16 stipulates that Party A has the right to refuse any transaction not handled in accordance with this Agreement and related operational procedures, and retains full recourse for economic losses caused by Party B’s intentional acts or negligence. Article 20 (Acceptance of Bank Cards) stipulates: Party B may accept payment by bank card only after confirming the following: 1. The bank card is intact and free from any form of alteration or modification; 2. The corresponding laser image on the card face is not damaged or blurred; 3. If an electronic card-accepting device is used, the card must be processed through the electronic device to complete the transaction; 4. If the communication line fails, Party B shall process the transaction manually as follows: (a) Obtain telephone authorization from Party A, and Party A shall record it; (b) Imprint the overseas bank card onto a sales slip, and fill in the amount, date, and other elements; (c) Obtain the cardholder’s signature and compare it with the signature on the back of the card; only after confirming they match may the transaction be processed; (d) Each manual sales slip shall include the following elements: bank card number, expiration date, transaction date, transaction amount, authorization number, Party B’s name and merchant number, cardholder signature, and document number. 5. The cardholder must be the person named on the card, and their name must match the name printed on the card face; if there is a signature on the back of the card, that signature must match the cardholder’s handwritten signature on the sales slip. 6. The card must be used on or after the start date displayed on the front of the card and on or before the expiration date; for cards issued by some financial institutions without a start date, the transaction must be processed through a dedicated electronic device or after authorization. 7. The signature panel on the card must not show obvious alteration or damage; 8. The card number on the front of the card must match the number printed on the back and the number printed on the sales slip; 9. If Party B uses an electronic card-accepting device, it shall process overseas bank card transactions online, and the cardholder need not present identification; if online processing is not possible due to device, network faults, or other reasons, Party B may also process manually; when processing manually, if Party B doubts the cardholder’s identity or the transaction, or if the merchant is a hotel-type merchant, Party B must require the cardholder to present identification and record the identification type and number. 10. For bank cards without embossed card numbers, the transaction must be processed by swiping the card through a dedicated electronic device. Article 23 (Reconciliation, Settlement, and Error Handling) stipulates: Party B shall strictly operate in accordance with the electronic device transaction processing procedures. Party A shall provide settlement services based on the transaction data transmitted by Party B and other instructions from Party B. After receiving the transaction data transmitted by Party B, Party A shall be responsible for timely processing. For amounts Party A determines to be normal transactions, Party A shall promptly transfer the funds to Party B’s designated account. After receiving an inquiry letter from Party A regarding a transaction, Party B must reply with all required materials within the time limit requested by Party A. Article 24 (Account Handling under Special Circumstances) stipulates: In any of the following circumstances, Party A has the right to deduct the relevant amounts from subsequent transaction funds generated between Party A and Party B, and has the obligation to inform Party B: (1) Party A discovers that Party B, when processing overseas bank card transactions, failed to retain the cardholder’s signature, the cardholder’s signature is clearly mismatched, or there are erroneous transactions such as duplicate charges that violate this Agreement; (2) The sales slip items are inaccurate or have not been confirmed by the cardholder or the issuing bank... Article 28 (Imposition of Surcharges on Cardholders and Cash Payments) stipulates that the charge for goods or services has been included in the sales slip document paid by bank card, and Party B shall not separately require the cardholder to make any form of payment. Appendix: (Definition of Terms) "Overseas card acquiring business" refers to the process by which Bank of China, as the card-acquiring bank, provides fund advances, business training, and risk prevention for legitimate institutions, and obtains payment from overseas issuing banks through international card organizations. "Manual slip" refers to a bank card transaction voucher produced and filled in manually using an imprinter.

From July 20, 2009, the defendant Tanyuan Road Business Department (originally named Kaiyue Building Business Department) leased from the plaintiff New Center Hotel an office in the business center and one position at the reception desk for ticketing and travel business. The parties signed a "Business Center Office Lease Contract" and a "Supplementary Agreement." The contract stipulated that the lessor ensures that the lessee is the hotel’s sole ticketing and travel service outlet during the lease term, that hotel guests’ travel ticketing and tour bus rental matters are given priority to the lessee; that the lessee does not separately pay the hotel any commission for hotel guests’ travel ticketing and car bookings; that the lessor provides uniform uniforms to the lessee; and that the lessee provides ticketing, car booking, and consultation services to hotel guests. After signing the contract, the Tanyuan Road Business Department began providing ticketing and travel services at the New Center Hotel’s business center. On the afternoon of December 15, 2009, Beijing time, the New Center Hotel’s reservation department received an email from a foreign customer named Steven (email: sobconsultant@gmail.com), inquiring whether the reservation department could book air tickets for him from Tokyo Narita International Airport to Singapore Changi Airport, and asking whether credit card payment was accepted. The reservation department replied asking whether he would first book a hotel room. Steven said he had not booked a room and wanted to book a ticket first before booking a room, and inquired whether they could help him book a ticket from FORST to China. The reservation department then replied: "Yes, we can book the ticket for you first, but if you pay by credit card, we will charge a commission of 18% of the total ticket price. If you cancel the ticket, a corresponding commission will also be charged. If you need us to make the reservation, please provide the booking details. Attached is our credit card payment authorization form. Please send a copy of the front and back of your credit card. Thank you!" Steven then sent three flight booking details to the reservation department. The reservation department replied: "We are sorry, after confirming with the reservation department manager, the reservation department cannot provide ticket booking services at this time. If you still need to book tickets, you can directly contact Suzhou Culture International Travel Service. Their business department has an office in our hotel. You can send your ticket booking details to Miss Li of the travel agency; her email is: tour163@gmail.com. She can help you book." At the same time, the reservation department forwarded the above emails between the parties to the Tanyuan Road Business Department (email: tour163@gmail.com) and informed Steven of the telephone numbers of Miss Li and Miss Teng of the Tanyuan Road Business Department. After contact, on December 17, 2009, the Tanyuan Road Business Department booked tickets for this customer, with payment by credit card. The customer sent copies of the front and back of the credit card and a filled-in credit card payment authorization form (authorized to Cultural International Travel Company, containing information such as credit card type, cardholder name, credit card number, expiration date, and CVV code) to the Tanyuan Road Business Department. Since the Tanyuan Road Business Department did not have its own electronic card-swiping device (i.e., POS machine), it submitted the above materials to the New Center Hotel, where the POS machine operator manually entered the credit card information into the POS machine to process the credit card transaction. From December 17 to December 22, 3 credit card transactions arose from the customer’s ticket bookings. On December 29, the customer sent three more ticket booking details to the New Center Hotel reservation department, which forwarded the email to Teng Jinyan of the Tanyuan Road Business Department (email: tenginyan8013@hotmail.com), asking to reply directly to Steven. Thereafter, the customer directly contacted the Tanyuan Road Business Department and successively booked tickets, resulting in 22 ticket booking transactions, using the New Center Hotel’s POS machine for 22 credit card transactions.

The credit card transactions involved in this case totaled 25 transactions, with a total amount of RMB 1,007,363, spanning from December 17, 2009, to January 29, 2010. All payments were made by customer Steven using different credit cards and cardholder authorizations through "card-not-present, no-PIN" payment. Each booking amount ranged from RMB 6,013.70 to RMB 70,176.40. Among the 25 credit card transactions, after deducting the bank handling fee (0.6% of the transaction amount), the net amount of transactions 1-21 was RMB 834,530.59, which the plaintiff New Center Hotel had already paid to the defendant Tanyuan Road Business Department after receiving payment from BOC Suzhou Branch. Transactions 22-25 had not yet been paid.

On January 21, 2010, Bank of China Suzhou Branch forwarded to the plaintiff Xindi Center a notice from the East China Center of BOC Financial Services Co., Ltd. requesting the submission of sales slips for the questioned transactions, which involved items 3 and 6 in the above table. On January 26, Bank of China Suzhou Branch again requested the submission of sales slips, involving item 10 in the above table. On January 29, Bank of China Suzhou Branch forwarded another notice, stating that it had received a notice from VISA International that Xindi Center had two questioned transactions of significant amounts in December 2009, involving items 2 and 4 in the above table, and requested the merchant to provide the relevant sales slips, invoices, hotel stay and consumption records, and to investigate the transactions. The notice also reminded the merchant that the occurrence of multiple questioned transactions within a short period reflected the merchant's very weak vigilance against problematic cards, indicating that it had become a target of counterfeit card gangs, and that most of the counterfeit cards discovered were foreign credit cards. Therefore, it requested that security inspection procedures be strengthened to prevent the continued occurrence of fraudulent card transactions. On January 29, 2010, after receiving the above notice, Xindi Center informed the defendant, the Ta Yuan Road Business Department, which then ceased its business with the customer. Thereafter, Bank of China Suzhou Branch successively requested the submission of sales slips for the remaining twenty credit card transactions.

On July 6, 2010, Bank of China Suzhou Branch issued a notice of chargeback for dishonored transactions to the plaintiff Xindi Center, stating that, according to the messages from the Bank of China payment and settlement system, it had made a recourse claim for a refund of foreign card charges totaling RMB 558,975, and would process a debit accounting entry from the funds held in suspense for Xindi Center's transactions.

During the litigation process, on September 8, 2010, Bank of China Suzhou Branch issued a detailed statement of bank deductions, clarifying that as of September 25, 2010, the total amount deducted was RMB 827,955.28 (the actual transaction amount was RMB 832,953.00), all resulting from transactions not authorized by the cardholders. On October 8, 2010, Bank of China Suzhou Branch again notified the plaintiff Xindi Center: as of August 5, it had received twenty debit advices for foreign card chargebacks from the issuing banks and had processed the refunds accordingly. There were still five foreign card transactions for which no chargeback refund notice had been received from the issuing banks. For four of these transactions, the number of days since the issuing bank initiated the chargeback inquiry had exceeded 180 days. According to the international organization's clearing and chargeback rules, a total of RMB 159,377.96 for these four transactions was credited to Xindi Center's hotel account. These four transactions correspond to items 5, 14, 15, and 24 in the above table. During the trial, Xindi Center confirmed that the transaction proceeds for item 19 in the above table had also exceeded the 180-day inquiry period, and Bank of China Suzhou Branch had already credited this amount to Xindi Center's account.

Additional facts found at first instance: The defendant, the Ta Yuan Road Business Department, is a subordinate branch of the defendant Wenhua Guoji Travel Company. It was originally named Suzhou Wenhua International Travel Service Co., Ltd., Kaiyue Mansion Business Department, and was changed to its current name on October 15, 2009.

The People's Court of Huqiu District, Suzhou City, Jiangsu Province held at first instance:

First, the twenty-five ticketing transactions involved in this case occurred between the defendant, the Ta Yuan Road Business Department, and foreign clients, forming a ticket service contract relationship between them. During the performance of this contract, the Ta Yuan Road Business Department used the plaintiff Xindi Center's POS terminal for card-swipe transactions. In essence, the Ta Yuan Road Business Department entrusted Xindi Center to collect airfare payments from the foreign clients, thereby forming a mandate contract relationship between the two parties. Xindi Center performed the entrusted collection without charging any fees or commissions from the Ta Yuan Road Business Department, constituting a gratuitous mandate. The actions of the受托人 (mandatary) in handling the mandated affair should be legally borne by the委托人 (mandator). On the one hand, the property obtained by the mandatary in handling the mandated affair should be transferred to the mandator, i.e., for the five successfully completed transactions in this case (net of bank charges), Xindi Center should pay the amount to the Ta Yuan Road Business Department. On the other hand, any losses arising from the mandated affair should be borne by the mandator. If such losses are caused by the mandatary's gross negligence, the mandatary should also bear corresponding legal liability. Specifically, for the twenty chargebacks in this case (including bank charges) resulting from the issuing banks' refusal to pay, these constitute losses arising from the entrusted collection matter and should first be borne by the mandator, the Ta Yuan Road Business Department. If Xindi Center was grossly negligent, it should bear liability for the corresponding losses.

Second, the plaintiff Xindi Center was grossly negligent in the process of collecting the airfare payments. The reasons are as follows: 1. The method of payment agreed upon between the Ta Yuan Road Business Department and Xindi Center for collecting the airfare was the "card-not-present, no-PIN" payment method via credit card. The so-called "card-not-present, no-PIN" method refers to a payment method where an operator manually enters the relevant credit card number using the keys on a POS terminal to obtain authorization for a credit card transaction through the network. This method does not involve reading credit card information through a card slot, and therefore does not require the physical credit card or PIN, nor does the cardholder need to be present. The operator can verify the credit card number, cardholder name, signature, CVV code, and other relevant information by telephone, fax, or other means, and then manually input the card details for the transaction. Although this payment method complies with the provision in the bank card agreement that transactions must be completed through an electronic device that accepts bank cards, and is a legally permissible credit card transaction method, it carries a higher transaction risk compared to the method where the cardholder swipes the card in person through the card slot, as it is impossible to verify the authenticity of the credit card or signature during the transaction process. 2. Xindi Center had entered into a bank card agreement with Bank of China Suzhou Branch for cooperation in processing foreign card transactions. According to the bank card agreement, the personnel responsible for the POS terminal must receive professional training from Bank of China Suzhou Branch before they can handle transactions and must strictly comply with the acceptance operating procedures. Therefore, the operators at Xindi Center were all professionally trained and should have a high degree of mastery of the relevant professional knowledge regarding acceptance conditions, operating procedures, risk prevention and control for foreign bank card transactions. They should have been aware of the transaction risk associated with the "card-not-present, no-PIN" payment method. 3. In this case, Xindi Center did not provide the Ta Yuan Road Business Department with a corresponding warning regarding this payment risk and its potential consequences. Parties should adhere to the principle of good faith and fulfill obligations of notification, assistance, confidentiality, etc., according to the nature, purpose, and trade practices of the contract. In handling the entrusted collection matter, Xindi Center failed to exercise the requisite duty of care by not warning the mandator of the payment risk it should have been aware of. Its conduct constituted gross negligence.

Third, the conduct of the defendant, the Ta Yuan Road Business Department, was the primary cause of the loss, having a greater causal force in the occurrence of the loss; the negligent conduct of the plaintiff Xindi Center was a secondary cause of the loss, having a lesser causal force. In this case, analyzing the respective roles of the conduct of Xindi Center and the Ta Yuan Road Business Department in causing the chargeback losses requires examining the entire process from beginning to end. On the one hand, after receiving the airfare booking request from the foreign client, Xindi Center informed the Ta Yuan Road Business Department, which then directly contacted and negotiated the ticket booking with the client. Therefore, the ticketing transaction occurred between the Ta Yuan Road Business Department and the foreign client, not between Xindi Center and the foreign client. As the party to the underlying ticketing transaction, the Ta Yuan Road Business Department should have exercised the corresponding duty of care regarding the rights, obligations, and legal consequences determined by its contract. It was responsible for independently and prudently judging and deciding on important factors such as the selection of the transaction counterparty, the initiation and continuation of the transaction, the payment method, and transaction risks. It also had the obligation to review the identity and creditworthiness of the transaction counterparty, as well as the authenticity and credibility of the documents submitted. However, considering the circumstances of the twenty-five ticketing transactions, all the air tickets booked by the foreign clients were for international flights, with the designated payment method being credit card. Furthermore, the booking persons and cardholders were all different foreigners who were not guests staying at Xindi Center's hotel, indicating a higher transaction risk. The Ta Yuan Road Business Department proceeded with the ticketing transactions without carefully verifying the clients' identities, assessing their creditworthiness, or giving due consideration to these abnormal circumstances. The erroneous selection of the transaction counterparty was the decisive factor leading to the ultimate loss. On the other hand, the Ta Yuan Road Business Department was not a special merchant of the bank and was unaware of the above-mentioned bank card agreement. Its personnel had not received professional training regarding the acceptance, settlement procedures, and risk control for foreign card transactions, and thus had a low level of relevant professional knowledge. Consequently, they lacked awareness of the transaction risk associated with the "card-not-present, no-PIN" payment method. Xindi Center's failure to provide the due warning regarding this payment risk led the Ta Yuan Road Business Department to believe that the transaction was complete once the acquiring bank paid the ticket amount, thereby affecting its judgment regarding the creditworthiness and transaction security of the ticket-booking clients and contributing to the occurrence of the event. This was a secondary cause of the loss, having a lesser causal force.

In conclusion, the court held that, considering the degree of causal force and the degree of fault, the plaintiff Xindi Center was grossly negligent in handling the entrusted collection matter. However, this negligent conduct had a lesser causal force on the resulting loss. Taking into account the fact that the mandate was gratuitous, the court, in its discretion, determined that Xindi Center should bear 20% of the loss. Therefore, for the chargeback losses (including bank charges incurred for the transactions) totaling RMB 832,953 caused to Xindi Center due to the issuing banks' refusal to pay, the defendant, the Ta Yuan Road Business Department, should bear RMB 666,362.40 (i.e., 80% of the loss), and Xindi Center should bear RMB 166,590.60 (i.e., 20% of the loss). Regarding the main claim, the court held that, after deducting bank charges, the actual amount of the twenty-five transactions was RMB 1,001,318.82 (RMB 1,007,363 * 99.4%). The amount of loss to be borne by the Ta Yuan Road Business Department was RMB 666,362.40. Therefore, the amount Xindi Center should pay to the Ta Yuan Road Business Department is RMB 334,956.42 (RMB 1,001,318.82 - RMB 666,362.40). Given that Xindi Center had actually paid RMB 834,530.59 to the Ta Yuan Road Business Department, the Ta Yuan Road Business Department should pay Xindi Center RMB 499,574.17 (RMB 834,530.59 - RMB 334,956.42) plus interest (calculated at the bank's benchmark lending rate for the corresponding period from the date of filing the lawsuit until the effective date of the judgment). Additionally, as the Ta Yuan Road Business Department is a branch established by the defendant Wenhua Guoji Travel Company without independent legal personality, Wenhua Guoji Travel Company shall bear supplementary liability for the portion of the above debt of the Ta Yuan Road Business Department that cannot be satisfied. Regarding the counterclaim, the court held that the transaction amounts included in the counterclaim request correspond to items 22, 23, and 24 in the transaction list. Among these, items 22 and 23 were charged back by Bank of China Suzhou Branch due to unauthorized transactions, while item 24 was successfully processed. These three transactions were all included in the resolution of the main claim. Based on the overall calculation of the twenty-five transactions, the Ta Yuan Road Business Department still owed Xindi Center RMB 499,574.17. Therefore, Xindi Center does not need to make any separate payment for the transaction amounts included in the counterclaim request.

Accordingly, pursuant to Articles 60 and 406 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court of Huqiu District, Suzhou City, Jiangsu Province rendered the following judgment on June 3, 2011:

1. The defendant, the Ta Yuan Road Business Department, shall, within ten days after the effective date of this judgment, pay the plaintiff Xindi Center the amount of RMB 499,574.17 and interest (calculated at the bank's benchmark lending rate for the corresponding period from the date of filing the lawsuit until the effective date of the judgment).

2. The defendant Wenhua Guoji Travel Company shall bear supplementary liability for the portion of the debt specified in the preceding paragraph 1 owed by the defendant Ta Yuan Road Business Department that cannot be satisfied.

Court acceptance fee for the main claim: RMB 10,762, to be borne by the plaintiff Xindi Center in the amount of RMB 2,000, and by the defendants Ta Yuan Road Business Department and Wenhua Guoji Travel Company in the amount of RMB 8,762. Court acceptance fee for the counterclaim: RMB 1,288, to be borne by Wenhua Guoji Travel Company. If the obligation to pay a sum of money is not fulfilled within the period specified in the judgment, interest on the debt for the period of delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 129 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

Wenhua Guoji Travel Company, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, filed an appeal to the Suzhou Intermediate People's Court, stating: First, during the first instance proceedings, the court did not add Bank of China Suzhou Branch as a party to the proceedings, nor did it review the legality of Bank of China Suzhou Branch's deduction. The cause of this case originated from the write-off and deduction actions of Bank of China Suzhou Branch. Based solely on the evidence submitted by the appellee Xindi Center in the first instance, it was impossible to prove whether the above actions of Bank of China Suzhou Branch were lawful. If Bank of China Suzhou Branch was not entitled to debit the corresponding amounts, then Xindi Center should seek recourse against Bank of China Suzhou Branch. Second, the court of first instance erred in finding that the first-instance defendant, the Ta Yuan Road Business Department, used Xindi Center's POS terminal for card-swipe transactions, which established a mandate relationship whereby the Ta Yuan Road Business Department entrusted Xindi Center to collect the ticket payments. In fact, the Ta Yuan Road Business Department conducted its business operations under the name of Xindi Center's "Business Center". In Xindi Center's daily operations, guests needing to book tickets were always directed to the Business Center. The hotel had also placed a signboard at the concierge desk indicating "Tourism, Ticket Booking / Qingdao Business Center". The Ta Yuan Road Business Department functioned as the ticket booking service department that a five-star hotel like Xindi Center must have. Third, the court of first instance made an erroneous finding regarding the causal relationship between the conduct of the Ta Yuan Road Business Department and Xindi Center and the loss in this case. In this case, all card-swipe transactions were conducted by Xindi Center's hotel; the Ta Yuan Road Business Department did not participate. The control over the risks in this process should also have been managed by Xindi Center. However, the losses caused by Xindi Center's negligence and fault should be borne entirely by Xindi Center. Therefore, the court of first instance's finding that the conduct of the Ta Yuan Road Business Department was the primary cause of the loss and Xindi Center's conduct was a secondary cause was erroneous. Fourth, Xindi Center should bear full responsibility for the aggravation of the loss. In this case, Bank of China Suzhou Branch notified Xindi Center on January 21, January 26, and January 29, 2010, informing it of the problematic transactions and issuing a warning on January 29. Xindi Center only terminated the transactions on January 29. During this period, numerous card-swipe transactions occurred, resulting in losses exceeding RMB 200,000. These losses were caused by Xindi Center's fault and should be borne entirely by Xindi Center. The appellant therefore requested that the court of second instance set aside the judgment of first instance and render a new judgment according to law.

The appellee Xindi Center argued in its defense: First, it was unnecessary to join Bank of China Suzhou Branch as a third party in this case. The foreign bank card business contract between Bank of China Suzhou Branch and Xindi Center was genuine and valid, and the appellant Wenhua Guoji Travel Company did not dispute its authenticity during the first instance trial. According to Article 24 of this contract, if the sales slip was not confirmed by the cardholder, the bank had the right to debit the transaction amount. The bank debited the transaction amounts based on this provision, and there was no controversy. Therefore, it was unnecessary to join Bank of China Suzhou Branch in this case. Second, the court of first instance's determination of the business relationship between the parties was entirely correct. Wenhua Guoji Travel Company's assertion in its appeal that Xindi Center entrusted the first-instance defendant Ta Yuan Road Business Department with ticket booking business is completely wrong. When guests at Xindi Center hotel needed to book tickets, Xindi Center simply directed them to the Ta Yuan Road Business Department, where the guests and the Ta Yuan Road Business Department negotiated directly. If guests paid in cash, they also paid the Ta Yuan Road Business Department directly. The executor STEVEN in this case was not a guest of the hotel and did not stay at the hotel. The itinerary, dates, and passengers for the air tickets he booked were discussed directly with the Ta Yuan Road Business Department. Therefore, there was no fact of the hotel entrusting the purchase of tickets. It is clear that Xindi Center merely acted as an agent for the Ta Yuan Road Business Department in collecting airfare payments. The court of first instance correctly found this fact. Third, the Ta Yuan Road Business Department's failure to verify the identity, authorization letter, and credit card of the ticket purchaser was the decisive factor leading to the ultimate loss. Since the ticket purchaser directly contacted the Ta Yuan Road Business Department for the business, and the ticket purchaser first submitted the authorization letter and credit card to the Ta Yuan Road Business Department, the Ta Yuan Road Business Department's failure to properly conduct the verification directly led to the loss. Fourth, Wenhua Guoji Travel Company's assertion that Xindi Center should have controlled the occurrence of business after the bank's request for sales slips does not reflect the actual situation. In its cooperation with the hotel regarding credit card business, Bank of China Suzhou Branch frequently requested sales slips, not only for the business involved in this case. According to the business contract between the parties, the bank had the right to request sales slips at any time, not only when abnormal transactions occurred. Moreover, in the transactions disputed in this case, the bank also requested sales slips, and not all of these requests were for problematic transactions; some transactions were normal. Fifth, the court of first instance found that Xindi Center had gross negligence because it did not inform the appellant of the risk associated with the "card-not-present, no-PIN" transaction method. Although Xindi Center did not appeal, this finding by the court of first instance is inappropriate. The "card-not-present, no-PIN" method is a transaction method permitted by the bank. Therefore, it was perfectly acceptable for the Ta Yuan Road Business Department to conduct such transactions at Xindi Center. Xindi Center itself had conducted a large number of such transactions without any similar incidents occurring. As long as the cardholder's identity, the power of attorney, and the credit card are properly verified, such risks do not occur. Therefore, Xindi Center was not at fault, let alone grossly negligent. Xindi Center requests that the court of second instance correct this finding on this issue.

Upon trial, the Suzhou Intermediate People's Court confirmed the facts found by the court of first instance.

During the second instance, the court required the appellee, New Land Center, and the appellant, Cultural Travel Company, to provide supplemental explanations regarding the chargeback retrieval process after Bank of China Suzhou Branch refused payment. New Land Center stated in this regard: When the hotel's finance department received the bank's retrieval notice, it telephoned Cultural Travel Company, requesting that it prepare the documents required by the bank and fax them to the bank. The bank conducted retrievals on January 21, 26, and 29, 2010, and in February 2010, requesting information on the guests' card swiping, guest consumption details, and the circumstances of the POS machine use. On January 27, Cultural Travel Company provided the bank with an explanation regarding the borrowing of the POS machine and, on February 1, 2010, provided guest consumption materials. The bank also frequently conducted retrievals in the hotel's regular operations, and in the hotel's own card-swipe transactions, there had never been any deductions or write-offs by the bank. Even among these retrieval transactions involving Cultural Travel Company, some transactions had been paid normally. Cultural Travel Company stated in this regard: On January 29, 2010, after receiving the retrieval notice forwarded by New Land Center, on the same day, the bank sent personnel to the business department requesting documents related to the disputed transactions. The business department provided all original sales slips to the bank and, on January 29, 2010, reported the case to the Economic Investigation Detachment of the Suzhou Public Security Bureau. Cultural Travel Company described the operational procedure for the disputed transactions as follows: Customers sent ticket purchase requests to the business department via email, attaching authorization letters and bank cards as email attachments. The business department printed these out and handed them to New Land Center staff, who used the POS machine to swipe the card and printed out the sales slip. The original sales slip was given to the business department, and a copy was retained by New Land Center. New Land Center staff informed the business department that once the sales slip was printed from the POS machine, the swipe was successful, and the business department would issue the ticket to the customer. After issuing the ticket, the business department would periodically aggregate several recent transactions and go to the New Land Center finance department to settle accounts. After the New Land Center finance department verified the settlement details against the retained copies of sales slips, it would pay the relevant amounts to the business department's account.

Another fact found in the second instance: On February 28, 2011, Cultural Travel Company applied to the Suzhou High-tech Zone (Huqiu) Administration for Industry and Commerce to cancel the registration of the Tayuan Road Business Department. On March 2, 2011, the industry and commerce authorities completed the cancellation of the Tayuan Road Business Department.

The issues in dispute in the second instance of this case are: First, whether the entity that formed the ticket service contract with the foreign customers is the appellee, New Land Center, or the defendant at first instance, Tayuan Road Business Department; Second, what legal relationship arose from New Land Center's provision of a POS machine for credit card receipt and settlement operations with the Tayuan Road Business Department, and whether New Land Center should bear liability for the deductions related to the 20 disputed transactions; Third, if New Land Center should bear liability, the scope of such liability.

The Suzhou Intermediate People's Court held in the second instance as follows:

Regarding the first issue, the relevant ticket booking transactions involved in this case occurred between the defendant at first instance, Tayuan Road Business Department, and the foreign customers. Although the appellant, Cultural Travel Company, argued that the Tayuan Road Business Department leased space from the appellee, New Land Center, uniformly wore New Land Center uniforms, and placed a sign at the concierge desk stating "For travel and ticket booking, please go to the business center," which constituted an essential service of a five-star hotel, and that the foreign customers were also introduced by New Land Center, therefore the Tayuan Road Business Department acted under New Land Center's mandate in engaging in ticket booking transactions with the foreign customers, and New Land Center should bear the responsibility. However, in this case, when the foreign customers contacted New Land Center, New Land Center explicitly informed the customers that the hotel reservations department could not provide flight booking services, and suggested that the customers directly contact Suzhou Cultural Travel Company's business department at New Land Center, providing the foreign customers with the contact information of the Tayuan Road Business Department. New Land Center also forwarded the emails to the Tayuan Road Business Department. Ultimately, all ticket-related communications and negotiations were completed between the foreign customers and the Tayuan Road Business Department, and both parties were aware of the counterparty to the ticket service contract. Cultural Travel Company's description of the transaction process in the second instance also confirmed this. New Land Center's act of introducing the foreign customers' ticket booking business to the Tayuan Road Business Department constituted performance of the obligation under the parties' Supplementary Agreement to give priority to introducing ticket booking business to the lessee. The Tayuan Road Business Department provided flight ticket booking services to the foreign customers in its own name and became the subject of the ticket service contract. Therefore, the appellant's claim that the Tayuan Road Business Department was acting under New Land Center's mandate in engaging in ticket booking transactions with the foreign customers lacks legal and factual basis. The subject of the ticket service contract relationship was the Tayuan Road Business Department and the foreign customers.

Regarding the second issue, first, in terms of the credit card receipt and settlement conduct, the defendant at first instance, Tayuan Road Business Department, borrowed the appellee, New Land Center's, POS machine for operations, forming a de facto relationship of an unpaid mandate contract with New Land Center. In the process of providing flight ticket booking services to the foreign customers, because the Tayuan Road Business Department itself had not applied to install a POS machine with a bank, it borrowed New Land Center's POS machine for credit card receipt purposes when collecting payments via credit cards. In this case, when the foreign issuing bank refused payment due to the foreign customers' chargebacks, New Land Center had already paid to the Tayuan Road Business Department the amounts for 21 transactions for which the Tayuan Road Business Department had applied for payment, less the bank fees deducted. New Land Center did not charge any fees or commissions to the Tayuan Road Business Department for the use of the POS machine. Therefore, the Tayuan Road Business Department's entrustment of New Land Center to settle the relevant payments with the bank on its behalf constituted an unpaid mandate relationship. New Land Center, as the mandatory, in handling matters related to credit card payment requests and settlements, bore the legal consequences of its actions for the mandator, the Tayuan Road Business Department. Where the mandatory causes losses to the mandator due to intentional misconduct or gross negligence, the mandatory shall bear liability for compensation.

Second, the appellee, New Land Center, when performing the mandate of using the POS machine for "card-not-present, no PIN" payment requests, failed to exercise due care and the duty to warn of risks, and was grossly negligent. The "card-not-present, no PIN" payment method carries higher risks compared to swiping a card through the card slot. The Business Cooperation Agreement for the Acceptance of Overseas Bank Card Transactions between Bank of China and Special Merchants entered into between New Land Center and Bank of China Suzhou Branch specifically provided detailed provisions on the matters to be examined by special merchants when accepting overseas bank cards, acceptance conditions, and operational procedures for different payment methods. For example, Article 20 of the Agreement provides that when accepting an overseas credit card for swiping, a special merchant must verify that the bank card is intact, with no form of alteration or modification; verify that the corresponding laser image on the card surface is not damaged or blurred; and, under normal circumstances, use the bank card acceptance electronic device to complete the acceptance transaction. If, for example due to communication line failure, the special merchant carries out manual imprinting, it must obtain telephone authorization from the bank, which the bank records; imprint the overseas bank card on the sales slip, fill in the amount, date, and other elements, and obtain the cardholder's signature, which must be verified against the signature on the back of the card before acceptance. The agreement also clearly specifies that when a special merchant uses the bank card acceptance electronic device, it should accept overseas bank cards through online mode and need not require the cardholder to present identification; however, if manual imprinting is used, and there is doubt about the cardholder's identity or the transaction, or if the merchant is a hotel-type merchant, then the cardholder must be required to present identification, and the name and number of the identification document must be recorded. It can be seen that obtaining the qualification of a special merchant for overseas bank cards from the bank implies mastery of various credit card settlement methods, including "card-not-present, no PIN," operational procedures, and matters to be examined, as well as a certain level of professional knowledge and risk prevention capability. Moreover, operating methods such as manual imprinting and "card-not-present, no PIN" require stricter procedures for special merchants than online card-swipe operations. Overseas bank card settlement differs from ordinary mandate matters. Given the complexity and professionalism of international settlement operations, the trust placed by the Bank of China in New Land Center when granting it special merchant settlement qualification was based on confidence in New Land Center's risk prevention and control capabilities. Similarly, the trust placed in New Land Center by the defendant at first instance, Tayuan Road Business Department, when entrusting it with POS receipt matters was based on confidence in New Land Center's long-standing financial professional expertise in overseas credit card transactions. Therefore, New Land Center had a duty to carefully verify and warn of risks regarding credit card swiping, especially non-ordinary online card-swipe methods such as "card-not-present, no PIN." In this case, the fraudulent card transactions by the foreign customers could not have occurred without the "card-not-present, no PIN" settlement method via the POS machine. New Land Center, as the mandatory that had received professional training, possessed professional knowledge, and had been engaged in POS machine card-swipe and credit card payment operations for many years, failed to carefully verify the authorization letters, identity documents, and signatures for the 25 involved transactions, and also failed to warn the mandator, the Tayuan Road Business Department, of the risks associated with the "card-not-present, no PIN" payment method. Therefore, New Land Center was grossly negligent in handling the mandate matters. Consequently, New Land Center's claim that it had no fault and should not bear liability lacks factual and legal basis.

Regarding the third issue, first, due to the gross negligence of the appellee, New Land Center, it should bear secondary liability for the losses. With respect to the causes of the losses arising from the 20 disputed transactions where payment was refused, there were three factors: the fraudulent card transaction by the foreign customers, the conduct of the defendant at first instance, Tayuan Road Business Department, and the gross negligence of New Land Center. Each party should bear different liabilities based on the different degrees of causation of the losses. The fraudulent card transactions by the foreign customers were the most direct cause of the losses. The Tayuan Road Business Department's failure to screen and carefully assess the transaction counterparty during the transactions should bear primary liability for the losses. Over a short period of just over one month, from December 17, 2009, to January 29, 2010, the same overseas customer frequently ordered flight tickets between different countries through the Tayuan Road Business Department via email, totaling 25 transactions, an average of nearly one per day. The individual amounts ranged from a minimum of over RMB 6,000 to a maximum of over RMB 70,000. Moreover, the orderers and cardholders were different foreigners who did not enter the country and frequently transited through international airports. The Tayuan Road Business Department did not entertain any reasonable suspicion regarding this abnormal situation, failed to carefully review the customer's identity and creditworthiness, and continued to transact with them. Therefore, the Tayuan Road Business Department's inadequate scrutiny of the transaction counterparty was the primary cause of the losses and should bear primary liability. On the other hand, as for the Tayuan Road Business Department, it had not received specialized training as a special merchant for international credit cards and had limited professional knowledge of overseas card acceptance, settlement procedures, and risk control. New Land Center, as the mandatory for receiving payments via overseas cards, failed to carefully review and warn of risks regarding "card-not-present, no PIN" transactions, and this was a secondary cause of the losses from the 20 refused payment transactions.

Second, in this case, the appellee, New Land Center, did not fail to notify in a timely manner, thereby causing an expansion of the losses. Bank of China Suzhou Branch issued retrieval notices to New Land Center on January 21 and January 26, 2010. New Land Center notified the defendant at first instance, Tayuan Road Business Department, and on January 27, 2010, the Tayuan Road Business Department issued a statement to Bank of China Suzhou Branch regarding the borrowing of New Land Center's POS machine. On January 29, 2010, Bank of China Suzhou Branch again issued a notice to New Land Center, which stated: "The merchant has experienced multiple problem transactions in a short period, reflecting a very weak alertness to problematic cards and having become a target of counterfeit card syndicates. Additionally, most counterfeit cards recently discovered are foreign credit cards. ... It is required to strengthen security inspection procedures to prevent further counterfeit card transactions." New Land Center notified the Tayuan Road Business Department on the same day it received the notice. Bank of China Suzhou Branch also specifically went to the Tayuan Road Business Department to request documents related to the disputed transactions, and the Tayuan Road Business Department reported the matter to the public security authorities on the same day. Therefore, during the process of the bank's retrieval in this case, New Land Center already notified the actual transaction subject, the Tayuan Road Business Department, in accordance with the relevant requirements of Bank of China Suzhou Branch to provide the transaction vouchers needed for the retrieval. And when Bank of China Suzhou Branch warned of the existence of counterfeit card issues, it notified the Tayuan Road Business Department on the same day. The appellant, Cultural Travel Company's claim that New Land Center's failure to notify in a timely manner caused an expansion of the losses, and that New Land Center should bear full liability for the expanded portion, lacks sufficient evidence and is not sustained.

In light of the above, the court of first instance, after comprehensively considering the fault and causation of each party regarding the losses, and taking into account that the appellee, New Land Center's, receipt of payments under the mandate was unpaid, determined that it was not inappropriate to order New Land Center to bear 20% of the losses from the issuing bank's refusal of payment.

Furthermore, according to Article 24 of the Business Cooperation Agreement for the Acceptance of Overseas Bank Card Transactions between Bank of China and Special Merchants entered into between the appellee, New Land Center, and Bank of China Suzhou Branch, it is expressly agreed that where the items on the sales slip are inaccurate or have not been confirmed by the cardholder or the issuing bank, Bank of China Suzhou Branch has the right to deduct the amounts involved in the disputed transactions from New Land Center's subsequent transaction payments. The appellant, Cultural Travel Company, also confirmed the authenticity of the Business Cooperation Agreement for the Acceptance of Overseas Bank Card Transactions between Bank of China and Special Merchants. Combined with the Bank Deduction Details and the Bank Deduction Write-off Details provided by New Land Center, it can be determined that Bank of China Suzhou Branch has already deducted the relevant amounts for the disputed transactions from New Land Center. This case actually concerns the allocation of losses suffered by New Land Center and Cultural Travel Company during the performance of the mandate. New Land Center has provided evidence to prove that the losses indeed exist. Therefore, Cultural Travel Company's appellate claim that Bank of China Suzhou Branch should be added as a party is not supported.

In summary, the factual findings of the original judgment were clear, and the application of the law was correct. The appellant, Cultural Travel Company's, appellate claims lack legal and factual basis and are not sustained. In this case, the circumstance that the defendant at first instance, the Tayuan Road Business Department, was canceled by the industry and commerce authorities constitutes new facts. Furthermore, the Tayuan Road Business Department was a branch without independent legal personality established by Cultural Travel Company. After its cancellation by Cultural Travel Company, the relevant liability should be borne by Cultural Travel Company. Therefore, the relevant liable subjects in the original judgment are adjusted in accordance with the law.

Accordingly, the Suzhou Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with Article 60 and Article 406 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 153, Paragraph 1, Subparagraph (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, on November 30, 2011, rendered the following judgment:

1. The civil judgment (2010) Hu Shang Chu Zi No. 0457 of the Huqiu District People's Court of Suzhou is hereby reversed.

2. The appellant, Cultural Travel Company, shall pay to the appellee, New Land Center, RMB 499,574.17 and interest (calculated from the date of filing of the lawsuit at the benchmark loan interest rate of the bank for the corresponding period until the date of this judgment's effectiveness) within ten days from the date this judgment takes effect.

The court acceptance fee for the original action is RMB 10,762, of which the appellee, New Land Center, shall bear RMB 2,000, and the appellant, Cultural Travel Company, shall bear RMB 8,762. The court acceptance fee for the original counterclaim is RMB 1,288, to be borne by Cultural Travel Company. The court acceptance fee for the second instance is RMB 10,762, to be borne by Cultural Travel Company.

This judgment is final.
